title: Inspect the Receipt Log
scenario: It is 10:20 AM. The invoice says 500 bolts; the PO agreed to 500. But were they actually delivered? The Receipt Log is the Receiving Desk's record of what physically arrived. Inspect the receipt for PO-7742 - the third leg of the match - and learn why a payment needs proof of delivery, not just a bill.
input: Goods receipt against PO-7742 | Quantity received: 500 | Receipt date: day-1 | Status: accepted | Posted by: Receiving Desk. This confirms the goods on PO-7742 arrived and were accepted - the physical event behind the invoice.
instructions: Read the Receipt Log as evidence the goods arrived, independent of the invoice.
Answer the four questions against the receipt and the workflow map.
Validate to mint the receipt source profile.

questions.prompt: What does the Receipt Log prove that the invoice cannot?

options.text: The price Beacon agreed to pay
That the goods physically arrived and were accepted

questions.explain: An invoice is a request for payment; a receipt is evidence of delivery. Paying without a receipt means paying for goods that may never have shown up.

options.text: The Receiving Desk, when goods arrive
The AP Clerk, from the invoice

questions.explain: Separation of duties: the people who receive goods post the receipt, independent of the people who pay. That independence is what makes the receipt trustworthy evidence.

questions.prompt: The receipt shows 500 received and the PO ordered 500. What does that satisfy?
questions.explain: The quantity leg of the three-way match asks: did we receive what we ordered? 500 received equals 500 ordered, so the quantity match passes cleanly.

questions.prompt: Which step combines this receipt with the invoice and the PO?
questions.explain: The three-way match reads all three legs - invoice, PO, and receipt - and only agrees when order, delivery, and bill line up. The receipt is the delivery leg.

copilotPrompt: Explain why a payables workflow needs a goods receipt: what it proves that an invoice cannot, who posts it and why that independence matters, and which step combines it with the invoice and PO.
successMessage: Receipt inspected. You now hold proof the goods arrived - the third leg the match needs.

sections.title: A bill is not a delivery
sections.body: The invoice asks to be paid; the receipt proves the goods actually arrived. The desk pays against evidence of delivery, not against a request alone.

sections.title: Separation of duties
sections.body: The Receiving Desk posts receipts; the AP desk pays. Because different people record delivery and payment, neither can quietly fabricate the other - a core financial control.

sections.title: The third leg of the match
sections.body: Order (PO), delivery (receipt), and bill (invoice) are three independent records. The three-way match only agrees when all three line up. This receipt is the delivery leg.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: Passing the inspection mints a receipt source profile: the quantity received, the accepted status, and who posted it - the evidence the match will read.

takeaway.heading: Receipt inspected
points: You answered the four questions: what the receipt proves, who posts it, the quantity match, and its first consumer.
A receipt is evidence of delivery - the desk pays against it, not against the invoice alone.
Separation of duties keeps receiving and paying independent, which is what makes the receipt trustworthy.
Your receipt source profile is stored - 500 received against 500 ordered, accepted, ready to match.
The workflow can now confirm the goods on every invoice were actually delivered.
